Create an evidence-bound execution baseline and concrete test protocol before revising discovery.

- Freeze the execution baseline and preservation boundary

- Define the complete interaction scenarios

- The source TRD is observed at its actual draft revision without a lifecycle mutation.

- Current source and preservation manifests exist.
- Mechanical baseline and actual-host baseline observations are classified.
- All C01–C14 scenarios and the manual-host protocol are concrete.

## Risks

- Preserve existing working-tree changes and report any unavailable host observation or conflicting Template update.

## TASK-001 - Freeze the execution baseline and preservation boundary

Reinspect the exact source TRD, approved plan and separate execution instruction, current source package, applicable guidance, working tree, mapping, and protected artifacts; retain a hash manifest and concise baseline before changing source files.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | `planned` |
| State reason | None |
| Skip authority | None |
| Requirements | REQ-014, REQ-015, REQ-019, REQ-020, REQ-022 |
| Design basis | None |
| Target artifacts | Verification/to-trd-intent-discovery/baseline.json, Verification/to-trd-intent-discovery/baseline.md |
| Dependencies | None |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | None |

### Risks

- The working tree already differs from Git HEAD; a reset would erase earlier work.
- The existing watcher may propagate valid source edits during the work; its running state must be observed and its service configuration must not be changed by inference.

### Acceptance criteria

- The record identifies the exact TRD revision, status and digest, exact plan approval and implementation authority, all baseline package hashes, current Git facts, and every protected path.
- The source helper, attribution and license are frozen as protected bytes under DEC-001; active-root, historical TRDs, existing Task records and unrelated plans retain their own baseline.
- The current Template mapping and pending update scope are inspected; unrelated pending work or a conflict receives a bounded stop rather than an overwrite.

### Planned verification

- Read the TRD and plan through their helpers and compare their exact identities and hashes with the authorized inputs.
- Inspect git status --short and current filesystem hashes without changing Git state.
- Run .venv/bin/python tools/template_update.py check and retain its actual JSON classification; inspect watcher status only as needed to understand automatic effects.
- Verify baseline.json accounts for the source package, active-root copy, mapped destinations, and every project.preserved_paths entry.

## TASK-003 - Define the complete interaction scenarios

Create the reusable C01–C14 scenario document with synthetic input sequences, expected visible behavior, requirement and acceptance links, and forbidden writes.

| Dependencies | TASK-001 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | None |

### Risks

- A scenario can conceal its own answer in the initial prompt or test only prepared document bodies.

### Acceptance criteria

- Every case C01–C14 has a concrete synthetic setup, user-message progression, expected response or pause, write boundary, and linked source requirement.
- Cases distinguish a complete prompt, partial or ambiguous answer, changed intent, prohibited follow-up, requested zero-requirement draft, legitimate product question, and exact approval.
- C01 includes differently worded variants; the source-resolvable fact is supplied through a readable fixture rather than a requested user recollection.

### Planned verification

- Compare every case with the source TRD REQ-017 criteria and the report's C01–C14 table.
- Review the first ambiguous prompt and turn boundaries to ensure the fixture does not pre-answer the material decision.
- Verify the scenario document does not claim execution, consent, or a completed behavior result.

## TASK-004 - Establish the manual host protocol and baseline observation

Define the manual Codex evaluation protocol and exercise representative ambiguous and complete requests with the existing package in a disposable baseline project.

| Field | Value |

| Status | `planned` |

| Requirements | REQ-004, REQ-008, REQ-017, REQ-018, REQ-020, REQ-022 |

| Target artifacts | Verification/to-trd-intent-discovery/host-protocol.md, Verification/to-trd-intent-discovery/baseline-interactions.md, SKILLS-depo/to-trd/tests/interaction-scenarios.md |
| Dependencies | TASK-001, TASK-002, TASK-003 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | None |

### Risks

- An in-memory host can retain stale instructions; the baseline package and actual session resources must be identifiable.
- A baseline failure is not presumed, and a passing baseline does not remove candidate verification obligations.

### Acceptance criteria

- The protocol defines disposable project creation, deliberate package selection, source and loaded-resource hashing, relevant host instructions, available model configuration, real user-turn boundaries, minimal evidence, and preservation checks.
- The baseline report records the actual ambiguous and complete responses without inventing a failing transcript or a root cause.
- The protocol uses manual existing-host sessions; an unavailable host exercise is a real blocker for that check and cannot be replaced by a static metadata claim.

### Planned verification

- Record the actual baseline skill entry/version and resources accessed in the host, then issue the synthetic ambiguous request and inspect the response and filesystem before supplying an answer.
- Run the specified complete request and record whether the fast path and draft approval boundary occur.
- Confirm only synthetic content and concise user-visible evidence are retained, with active-root and product installations unchanged.
